title: Norml WordPress Developer
audience: WordPress engineers maintaining new or inherited themes
actsOn: Theme source, editor components and release workflow
pitch: Build WordPress themes with explicit content architecture, reusable components, editor previews and verified releases.
problem: A new stack needs a coherent authoring and release workflow. An inherited theme needs changes that respect its existing architecture.
The package supplies both paths and separates code/schema deployment from live content ownership.
commands: Work on this inherited non-Sage theme
Add a block with an editor preview
Set up WordPress CI and staging-to-production gates

flow.d: Verify model, stack, roots and current policy.
Use Sage standards or retain the inherited architecture.
Compose content boundaries, components and editor previews.
Run relevant checks, responsive review and antipattern audit.
Use the approved exact-source deployment and recovery policy.

items.name: New Sage engineering
items.desc: Acorn/Blade/Tailwind/Vite guidance with project version checks.

items.name: Inherited theme changes
items.desc: Match current templates, ACF/native blocks and compiler.

items.name: Editor and CSS standards
items.desc: Block previews, reusable components and three CSS layers.

items.role: Metadata and legacy blocks with preview acceptance
Standalone release, artifact and rollback procedure

items: Project access, compatible runtime and optional ACF PRO licensing are supplied by the user.
Not a turnkey installer/deployer; samples must be adapted and verified.
No silent inherited framework/builder replacement or automatic production data overwrite.
UI/CI/provider examples are not live-executed by installing this package.
